title: Basis on Which a Resort Lodging Reservation Record Is Closed
content:
A Resort Lodging reservation record is closed only when the folio shows nothing left to collect and no deposit left standing against it. Both conditions are read off the collective's own record of the reservation before the record is closed, and the household's own account of what it has paid is not the authority for either.

Closing is the last write on the record and nothing is added to it afterwards; a household who finds a charge afterwards raises it with the finance team rather than at the desk.

A cancelled reservation closes once whatever is retained has been taken and whatever comes back has been returned; an unclaimed reservation closes once the unclaimed nights have been taken.

Lodging credit issued against a closed reservation keeps its own validity period and is spent against a later stay.

The collective keeps the folio of a closed reservation for the household to ask for, but never reopens it to add a charge that was missed at the time.

### The two conditions read together (hypothetical records)

A record showing nothing left to collect on the folio but a deposit still standing against the reservation satisfies one condition and not the other, and is not closed. A record showing no deposit standing but an amount still to collect likewise satisfies one and not the other, and is not closed. Only a record showing nothing left to collect and no deposit standing satisfies both.
